Fellowship pathway

The contribution ladder for executive intelligence.

Every member begins with access to the network. Fellowship levels recognize the executives who participate deeply, contribute original insight, help create the institution's intellectual property, and eventually become part of its legacy.

Explore Levels Back to Membership
Institutional signal Founding Fellow should still mean something twenty years from now.

The pathway is designed so recognition is earned through contribution, trust, intellectual leadership, and long-term executive influence.

Five levels

From accepted member to permanent institutional title.

The levels create aspiration without turning membership into a transaction. They mark contribution, leadership, and trust inside the Executive Intelligence Network.

Level 01 Executive Member

Everyone starts here.

Executive Members have been accepted into the network and are invited into the core rhythm of year-round executive intelligence.

Who they are

  • Accepted into the network
  • Invited to Executive Intelligence Sessions
  • Receives Quarterly Briefs
  • Receives the Annual Yearbook
  • Executive Directory access
  • Summit invitations

Expected contribution

  • Participate
  • Share perspectives
  • Complete occasional surveys
Level 02 Contributing Member

These are active participants.

Contributing Members are visible in the community because they show up, share meaningful experience, and help the network learn faster.

They have

  • Attended multiple sessions
  • Shared meaningful experiences
  • Participated in research
  • Engaged with the community

Additional benefits

  • Early invitations
  • Topic voting
  • Priority roundtables
  • Invitations to private discussions
Level 03 Executive Contributor

They help create the network's intellectual property.

Executive Contributors move from participation into authorship, facilitation, commentary, and mentorship.

They may

  • Lead a discussion
  • Participate on panels
  • Write executive commentary
  • Review quarterly briefs
  • Mentor newer members
  • Host a session

Benefits

  • Featured profile
  • Published contributor
  • Invitation to Leadership Council meetings
  • Research advisory opportunities
Level 04 Executive Fellow

This becomes prestigious.

Executive Fellows are leaders people know. They have given the network time, credibility, mentorship, and visible executive influence.

Requirements might include

  • Multiple years participating
  • Leading sessions
  • Published contributions
  • Mentoring
  • Significant executive influence

Benefits

  • Annual Fellow Dinner
  • Private strategy sessions
  • Invite-only leadership retreats
  • Opportunity to chair research initiatives
Level 05 Founding Fellow

Reserved for the first generation.

Founding Fellow is for the executives who helped build the institution. It is permanent, scarce, and meant to remain valuable decades from now.

Who they are

  • Executives who helped establish the network
  • Early builders of the institution's reputation
  • Leaders who shaped the first body of intelligence
  • Permanent title holders

Why it matters

  • Signals original contribution
  • Creates historical prestige
  • Anchors the network's founding generation
  • Gives future members something real to aspire to
Contribution badges

Recognition should show how someone contributes.

Levels describe overall standing. Badges describe the role an executive actually plays in the network, creating a more personal contribution profile.

Research

Research Contributor

Participated in executive research, interviews, surveys, or benchmark conversations.

Sessions

Discussion Leader

Moderated, framed, or led Executive Intelligence Sessions and private roundtables.

Reports

Publication Contributor

Quoted in reports or contributed field perspective to briefs, yearbooks, and executive commentary.

Growth

Mentor

Helped other executives think through AI leadership, organizational change, or implementation decisions.

Council

Council Member

Serves on a standing council and helps shape ongoing research, sessions, and community direction.

Summit

Summit Faculty

Leads flagship summit sessions, executive roundtables, or high-value member learning experiences.

Executive Impact Measure contribution without turning it into public points.

MOJO can maintain a private Executive Impact model that informs invitations, recognition, fellowship progression, and leadership opportunities. The exact weighting stays internal so public recognition feels earned, not gamed.
